summary.one_liner: tldr-pages is a community-maintained collection of simplified, example-driven help pages for command-line tools, meant as a friendlier complement to man pages.
summary.what_it_does: The project is a growing set of Markdown help pages covering common UNIX, Linux, macOS, FreeBSD, NetBSD, OpenBSD, SunOS, Android, Windows, Cisco IOS, and DOS command-line tools. Each page focuses on practical usage examples rather than exhaustive option descriptions. The README lists several official clients: a Python client (installed via pipx from PyPI), a Rust client (tlrc, installable via Homebrew, Cargo, or Winget), and a Node.js client that the README says has fallen behind in updates. It also points to a web client with offline PWA support, PDF versions of the pages (including translations in release assets), and community-made clients listed on the wiki. Contributors can add new commands, improve examples, work on requested pages, or translate content, all via pull requests.
use_cases: look up quick usage examples for a command-line tool
learn common options for tar, lsof, and similar commands
get simplified help instead of reading man pages
offline cheat sheets for shell commands
notable: Pages are short, example-first Markdown files rather than full manuals
Covers many platforms including Windows, Cisco IOS, DOS, and Android
Multiple official clients plus a web client with offline PWA support
Translations are available, with PDF versions for most languages
caveats: The Node.js client has fallen behind in updates, per the README
Pages are community-maintained, so coverage and accuracy vary
The web client link is missing from the README text provided
